approach: Use a prebuilt CSS theme for a quick start, or call the mat.theme Sass mixin for full control over color, typography, and density from a single include.
explanation: Angular Material 17+ ships a single Sass mixin, mat.theme, that generates both the color and typography CSS custom properties every Material component reads. Include it once, typically on html or body, after `@use '@angular/material' as mat;`. Prebuilt CSS themes (imported as a stylesheet in angular.json, e.g. @angular/material/prebuilt-themes/indigo-pink.css) remain available for projects that don't need a custom palette.
gotchas: mat.theme should be included exactly once per stylesheet scope — including it more than once duplicates every component's CSS custom properties.
A prebuilt theme stylesheet and mat.theme are mutually exclusive; using both at once produces conflicting custom property values.

Components that render outside the themed element's DOM subtree (e.g. into the cdk-overlay-container via a portal) still pick up the theme, because the custom properties live on html, not on a component's host element.
